chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked him about a man who buys from the tax collector (or agent) while he is being unjust (or oppressive), so he said: 'He buys from him.'

key_terms.الْعَامِلِ: The agent, tax collector, or governor's representative
key_terms.يَظْلِمُ: He is unjust or oppressive (in his calculations or duties)

ai.seo_question: Is a transaction valid if you buy from a tax collector who is unjust?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam establishes that the validity of a commercial transaction (*sahih*) is not contingent upon the moral integrity or justice of the seller, provided the essential conditions of the contract are met. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the external validity of the trade and the internal spiritual state of the parties, allowing believers to engage in necessary economic activities even with those who may be unjust in their broader conduct.
